questions.stem: In this question the answer to each part is a number.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the pH value of a neutral solution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give a pH value of a weakly acidic solution.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give the number of the Group in the Periodic Table that contains the elements that do not readily react.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Give the number of different elements present in glucose, $ \mathrm{C_{6} H_{1 2} O_{6}} $

questions.stem: The solubility of a solid depends on the solvent used.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State one other factor that affects the solubility.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A student wants to find the solubility of a salt in water. The steps in the student's method are not in the correct order. Step A gently heat the evaporating basin and solution to remove all the water Step B filter to obtain $ 5 0. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of saturated solution Step C record the mass of the evaporating basin and salt solution Step D record the mass of an empty evaporating basin Step E record the mass of the evaporating basin and the dry salt Step F put $ 5 0. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of water into a beaker Step G add the salt to the water a little at a time and stir until no more dissolves Step H pour the $ 5 0. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of saturated salt solution into the evaporating basin

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: The flowchart shows the correct order of some of the steps. Complete the flowchart by putting the remaining steps in the correct order.

questions.stem: When 10.0kg of a solid fuel is burned,the heat energy produced is $ 3. 2 8 \times1 0^{5} $ kJ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the heat energy, in kJ/mol, produced by the fuel. You should assume that the fuel is pure carbon. Give your answer to three significant figures. [for carbon, $ A_{\mathrm{r}}=1 2 $]

parts.label: b
parts.text: The fuel actually contains some impurities, including sulfur. There is 600g of sulfur in 20kg of fuel.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Calculate the percentage of sulfur in the fuel.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: When the fuel burns,the 600g of sulfur produces sulfur dioxide gas. $S + O _ {2} \rightarrow S O _ {2}$ Calculate the volume, in $ cm^{3} $ , of sulfur dioxide gas that would be produced at room temperature and pressure (rtp) when the fuel burns. [for a gas, molar volume = 24 dm $ ^{3} $ at rtp]

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: State the name of the environmental problem caused by sulfur dioxide in the atmosphere.

questions.stem: (a) Hand sanitiser liquids are used regularly to reduce the spread of infections. Three compounds P, Q and R are often present in these liquids. (i) What type of formula is shown for P? (ii) Compounds P, Q and R are members of the same homologous series. Give two properties of a homologous series. (iii) Name the homologous series that contains compounds P, Q and R. (iv) Give the name of compound Q. A a displayed formula B an empirical formula C a molecular formula D a structural formula

parts.label: b
parts.text: Diols and dicarboxylic acids react together in polymerisation reactions to form polyesters.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Explain the name given to the type of polymerisation that occurs in these reactions.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Complete the equation for the polymerisation reaction by giving the displayed formula of the repeat unit of the polymer.

questions.stem: This question is about the element phosphorus and some of its compounds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The atomic number of phosphorus is 15 Give the electronic configuration of an atom of phosphorus.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calcium phosphide is an ionic compound used in pest control. The formula of a calcium ion is $ \mathrm{C a}^{2+} $ Explain why the formula of calcium phosphide is $ \mathrm{C a}_{3} \mathrm{P}_{2} $

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calcium phosphide can be produced by heating calcium phosphate with carbon.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Complete the equation for the reaction. $\mathrm {C a} _ {3} \left(\mathrm {P O} _ {4}\right) _ {2} + \dots \dots \dots \dots \mathrm {C} \rightarrow \mathrm {C a} _ {3} \mathrm {P} _ {2} + \dots \dots \dots \dots \mathrm {C O}$

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Explain the role of carbon in the reaction.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Calcium phosphide reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide and phosphine, $ \mathrm{P H_{3}} $ Give a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Explain why calcium phosphide has a high melting point. You should refer to structure and bonding in your answer.

questions.stem: Iron metal was discovered several thousand years ago. Iron is produced industrially from iron(III) oxide by extraction using carbon. Sodium is a metal in Group 1 of the Periodic Table. Sodium was discovered by Sir Humphrey Davy in 1807. It is produced industrially by the electrolysis of sodium chloride.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain, using the reactivity series, why carbon can be used to extract iron from iron(III) oxide.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Suggest why sodium was not discovered until 1807.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The diagram shows a simplified version of the Downs cell, which can be used to produce sodium industrially. The electrolyte is molten sodium chloride.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Explain why the molten electrolyte conducts electricity.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: What is the formula of the cation in the electrolyte? A $ \mathrm{H^{+}} $ B $ \mathrm{Cl^{-}} $ C $ \mathrm{Na^{+}} $ D $ \mathrm{OH^{-}} $

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: During the production of sodium, small explosions can be heard. Explain why using sodium chloride that is not completely dry could cause these small explosions.

parts.label: b-iv
parts.text: Give ionic half-equations for the reactions at the anode and cathode. anode ... cathode

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the reactivity of metals in Group 1 increases from lithium to potassium.

questions.stem: A student is asked to find the concentration of a solution of nitric acid by doing a titration. The student is provided with sodium hydroxide solution with a concentration of $ 0.350\mathrm{mol/dm}^{3} $ These are the first four steps in the student's method. use a pipette to add exactly $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of the nitric acid solution to a conical flask placed on a white tile add a few drops of indicator to the flask use a burette to add sodium hydroxide solution to the flask until the indicator has changed colour record the volume needed for the indicator to change colour

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the reason for using the white tile.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Universal indicator is not a suitable indicator to use in a titration. Complete the table to show the name of a suitable indicator and its final colour in this titration.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student wants to obtain an accurate value for the volume of sodium hydroxide solution needed to neutralise the $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of nitric acid. Describe all the further steps the student should take.

parts.label: d
parts.text: This is a summary of the student's results. volume of $ \mathrm{H N O}_{3} $ used $ = 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ concentration of NaOH solution = 0.350 mol/dm $ ^{3} $ volume of NaOH solution needed for neutralisation $ = 1 8. 8 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ The equation for the reaction is $\mathrm {H N O} _ {3} + \mathrm {N a O H} \rightarrow \mathrm {N a N O} _ {3} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of NaOH that reacts. $\mathrm {a m o u n t o f N a O H} =$

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Determine the amount, in moles, of $ \mathrm{H N O_{3}} $ that reacts. $\mathrm {a m o u n t o f H N O} _ {3} =$

parts.label: d-iii
parts.text: Calculate the concentration, in mol/dm $ ^{3} $ , of the $ \mathrm{H N O}_{3} $ $\mathrm {m o l / d m ^ {3}}$

questions.stem: This question is about reactions involving nitrogen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a car engine, nitrogen reacts with oxygen to form nitrogen monoxide. The equation for the reaction is $\mathrm {N} _ {2} + \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {N O} \quad \Delta H = + 1 8 1 \mathrm {k J}$ Draw a labelled reaction profile diagram showing $ \Delta H $ and the activation energy for the reaction.

parts.label: b
parts.text: In the Haber process, nitrogen reacts with hydrogen to form ammonia. This equation represents the reaction. $\mathrm {N} \equiv \mathrm {N} + 3 \mathrm {H} - \mathrm {H} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {H} - \mathrm {N} - \mathrm {H}$ The table gives values of some bond energies.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Calculate the total amount of energy, in kJ, needed to break the bonds in the reactants.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Calculate the total amount of energy, in kJ, released in forming the bonds in the product.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Calculate the enthalpy change, $ \Delta H $ , for the reaction. You should include a sign in your answer. $\Delta H =$
